Optional summary:
Quick partner GTM alignment and unblock a stalled enterprise opportunity. Primary goals: clarify reseller integration steps (SSO, billing, lead registration), agree on pilot benchmark responsibilities, and establish immediate next steps to rescue a delayed deal with a mutual customer.

Topics covered:

- Pilot benchmark and performance expectations

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, Leo our solutions engineer, Jasmine CSM. Carlos, Nina, Samir, Liam — did I get that right?
[00:10] Carlos (Brightline): Yep that's right, Carlos here. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:14] Nina (Brightline): Nina — afternoon y'all.
[00:17] Samir (Brightline): Samir, CTO.
[00:18] Liam (Brightline): Liam O'Connor, RevOps. Sorry I'm late like two minutes.
[00:22] Maya: No problem. Quick agenda: integration checklist, who does the pilot benchmark, and then commercial mechanics so we can clear the stall on the NovaCare deal.
[00:29] Leo (Redwood): I'll jump in on the tech bits — we'll try to keep it light.
[00:33] [00:35] Leo: So high-level — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) deployments. For reseller scenarios you usually want either hosted with partner billing or Dedicated/Private for regulated customers. Which path is NovaCare leaning to?
[00:47] Carlos: They indicated VPC originally because of PHI concerns but I think they might accept a hosted plus strong encryption and KMS if the math works.
[00:56] Samir: Right, they want assurance on key custody and auditability. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:02] Maya: Totally. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO mentioned in the docs we shared. For key custody, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with HSM-backed KMS and options to integrate with a customer's KMS via federated keys — though there are limitations on full key ownership.
[01:18] Nina: That "federated keys" line — can you spell out the limitation? That was a blocker for procurement.
[01:23] Leo: Sure. In hosted mode, we can integrate via a tokenized flow and customer-managed keys for data-at-rest but we hold the runtime key material — it's ephemeral. So if the customer needs full on-prem HSM ownership with no cloud-side key material, they'd go Dedicated/Private.
[01:37] [01:40] Samir: Okay that helps. It's the auditors hunting for a provable separation.
[01:43] Maya: We can provide KMS policy templates and an audit log sample. I'll send those after.
[01:47] Carlos: Great. The other big issue is revenue — Brightline has been pushing hard on the commission structure for resellers. They want at least 18-20% net.
[01:56] Lily: [mislabel] -- (laugh)
[01:56] Maya: (laugh) noted. We typically work with tiered reseller margins plus deal registration credits. For enterprise we usually have a custom rebate.
[02:06] Liam: Can you explain the lead registration part? Their process broke because of missed credit on a lead and that stalled the close.
[02:12] Maya: Sure — our playbook is lead must be registered with CRMD id and date, and partner must attach partner_id to the opportunity in our portal. We then validate within 5 business days. Seems like in NovaCare case the partner registered late and the portal didn't have the correct partner account mapping.
[02:24] Carlos: Right that mismatch caused them to not get their referral credit so Brightline pulled back.
[02:29] Maya: We can waive backwards for this deal as an exception if we get confirmation by EOD Friday. But to avoid repeat, we'll share the lead registration SOP.
[02:37] [02:40] Nina: That exception is crucial — otherwise Brightline won't re-engage the AE.
[02:44] Maya: Understood. We'll commit to exception and email confirmation.
[02:48] Leo: On the pilot benchmark — we propose Redwood runs a 3-step check: 1) latency/throughput on Brightline input traces, 2) cost per 1k tokens with quantized runtime, 3) failover simulation if a zone goes down. We can share a simple script and the benchmark sheet.
[03:06] Samir: We can share anonymized traces but need to scrub PHI. How heavy an obfuscation should we do?
[03:12] Leo: Token-level PII removal is fine — we only need the length distributions, conversation patterns, and pk-inference load. Redacted is fine.
[03:20] Samir: Okay we'll work on a scrubbed sample.
[03:24] [03:30] Maya: Timeline — Leo runs the benchmark, posts results; if it meets the SLA we'll propose a 6-week pilot on Dedicated or Private, depending on the KMS outcome.
[03:38] Liam: On commercial side, Brightline asked for a standard reseller agreement + a short SOW for the pilot. Can you send drafts?
[03:45] Maya: Yes, I'll send a redline-friendly MSA and a pilot SOW template after this call.
[03:49] Carlos: Also want to confirm training for their sales team — a partner-facing product demo and battle cards.
[03:55] Jasmine (Redwood): We have a partner enablement kit — demo deck, one-pager, objection handling docs. I'll own the enablement deliverable.
[04:02] [04:10] Nina: There was a comment earlier about endpoint control — Brightline reps want to know if they can surface a branded UI or must use Redwood UI.
[04:16] Leo: For hosted we expose APIs and webhooks; partners can build a branded UI on top. For Dedicated/Private, we can white-label some console elements subject to enterprise legal. There are minimum support fees.
[04:27] Maya: Quick note on fallback: if the dedicated cluster becomes constrained, our routing policy can fall back to a smaller quantized model or to a hosted pool subject to tenant-policy. That was an ask from the product team at NovaCare — they want graceful degradation not hard errors.
[04:43] Samir: Can that fallback preserve KV cache to avoid big latency spikes?
[04:48] Leo: Not fully across different model variants. If you fallback across regions or model families, we rebuild KV cache. There will be a short warm-up. We can however do prefix caching to reduce cold start penalties.
[04:58] [05:05] Carlos: There was also vendor concern — they saw CloudServeAI offering reseller margins a bit higher, and their SSO integration was more turnkey. How do we compete?
[05:14] Maya: We lean into predictable economics and show the benchmark numbers. We also offer more flexible deployment and can move them to Dedicated with reserved capacity for stable latency, which CloudServe might not offer at the same price.
[05:24] Nina: Brightline sales want a simple slide comparing net cost and latency between Redwood hosted vs CloudServe hosted. Can you put that together?
[05:31] Leo: We'll produce an apples-to-apples comparison using the benchmark sheet and target the top three scenarios.
[05:36] Maya: Ok I want to call out one process change to avoid future stalls: add an automatic workflow where if partner claim is mismatched, RevOps is notified and we lock a temporary credit hold pending manual review. Liam, would that work?
[05:48] Liam: That's doable; we can add a soft hold and a 72-hour SLA for resolution. I'll follow up on the implementation details.
[05:55] [06:02] Maya: Great. Wrap — recap and next steps. I will: send the lead registration SOP and exception confirmation tonight, attach MSA + SOW templates, and the co-sell one-pager. Leo will start the benchmark pending scrubbed traces. Samir will share SSO/KMS details. Jasmine will schedule the partner enablement demo. Liam will confirm commission slab and RevOps workflow.
[06:22] Carlos: Thanks everyone — if we can get the exception and the benchmark copy, we'll relaunch NovaCare next week.
[06:27] Maya: Perfect. Any final Qs?
[06:30] Nina: One last ask — can you include a short FAQ addressing data residency and audit logs? That would help the procurement team.
[06:36] Maya: Yes, will include that.
[06:39] Samir: Cool, thanks.
[06:41] [06:42] End meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: there were a few mislabels and an accidental speaker tag at 01:56; some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Dedicated" inconsistently. Natural disfluencies present.
